title: Every field of characteristic p has a p-basis
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, $k$ a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic $p$, and $k^p=\{a^p:a\in k\}$, a subfield of $k$. Then there is a family $(t_i)_{i\in I}$ of elements of $k$ (a $p$-basis of $k$) such that the monomials $t^E=\prod_{i\in I}t_i^{e_i}$, where $E=(e_i)_{i\in I}$ runs over the families of integers $0\le e_i<p$ with $e_i=0$ for all but finitely many $i$, form a basis of $k$ as a vector space over $k^p$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Definition Tag 07P1 (definition-p-basis, item 2) and Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), sentence 'In particular, the field K has a p-basis over k', for the extension F_p -> k (then kK^p = k^p), and its proof (Zorn's lemma, the claim on maximal p-independent subsets); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: Take the base field $\mathbf F_p$ and the empty family in $k$. There is exactly one finitely supported exponent function on the empty set, namely zero; its monomial is $1$. This singleton family is linearly independent over $\mathbf F_p k^p$, since a coefficient times $1$ vanishes only if that coefficient vanishes.

source.place: More on Algebra, Tags 07P1 and 07P2, p-basis extension assertion specialized to the empty family over the prime field

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-p-independent-extends-to-p-basis] to $\mathbf F_p \subseteq k$ and the empty family. It returns an index set $J$, a family $y_j$, and the bounded monomial basis indexed by exponent functions on $\varnothing \sqcup J$. The coefficient field is $\mathbf F_p k^p=k^p$, because Frobenius fixes the prime field.

proof.text: Use $I=\varnothing \sqcup J$ and the combined family. The basis and its monomial evaluation identity supplied by the extension theorem are exactly the required witnesses.

lean.statement: theorem exists_p_basis (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p] : ∃ (I : Type u) (t : I → k) (b : Module.Basis {E : I →₀ ℕ // ∀ i : I, E i < p} (IntermediateField.adjoin (ZMod p) (Set.range (fun x : k => x ^ p))) k), ∀ E, b E = E.val.prod (fun i e => t i ^ e)
